question: We have observed with regret the participation of the Turkish Foreign Minister, Mr Hakan Fidan, in the European Union’s Foreign Affairs Council and the unacceptable demands he put forward in the course of its proceedings. We would point out that this is at the very time when, in Cyprus, the illegal occupation by Türkiye continues, backed up by the threat of arms.
These developments circumvent the EU itself and contravene its fundamental values, such as freedom of movement and respect for sovereign rights.

We find it difficult to understand how the participation of Mr Fidan is allowed, when his country not only does not recognise all the Member States of the EU but, at the same time, systematically violates the principles and rules of the Union, for example by infringements relating to the customs union and the unfair competition caused by the Turkish embargo. 1.
Can you explain to us what justification there can be for Mr Fidan’s participation in meetings of the Foreign Affairs Council under these circumstances?
When a state shows disrespect for the European Union by not recognising one of its Member States, which the Republic of Cyprus is, how can it participate in the Union’s institutions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.1.2025) The Foreign Minister of Türkiye, Hakan Fidan, did not participate, on 29 August 2024, in the European Union’s Foreign Affairs Council. He attended an informal reunion of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of EU Member States.

This informal format, which does not count as a formal reunion of an EU institution, gives a good opportunity for exchanges with non-EU Ministers of Foreign Affairs. The High Representative/Vice-President and European Commission’s Joint Communication of November 20231 included the participation of the Turkish Foreign Minister to such an informal meeting as one of its recommendations.
The European Council of April 2024 tasked Coreper to advance work on the recommendations of the Joint Communication in line with previous European Council conclusions2.

The EU is fully committed to a comprehensive settlement to the Cyprus problem, within the United Nations (UN) framework, in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and in line with the principles on which the EU is founded and the EU acquis. The EU has made repeatedly clear that it remains crucial that Türkiye commits and contributes to such a peaceful settlement, including its external aspects.
Türkiye must normalise its relations with the Republic of Cyprus and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all EU Member States3.
